fatal_errors: The proposed FSP treatment does not reconstruct the SPS-consolidated HEA electrode and electrospark-deposition intervention.
The substrate, alloy composition, processing window, and deposition architecture differ from the target system.
No prior evidence is cited even though supporting evidence was explicitly requested.
Hardness, wear, corrosion, and hot-cracking improvements are asserted without data; the target study did not test corrosion, wear, or aggressive-environment performance.

The claim that processing below 0.5Tm will produce dynamic recrystallization and in situ mechanical alloying in austenitic stainless steel is insufficiently justified and may be physically inconsistent for the stated parameter range.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the general repair problem and offers a potentially useful solid-state alternative to fusion welding, so it is scientifically plausible at a broad level. However, it misses essentially every defining feature of the hidden study: mechanically alloyed CrFeNiMo-family powders, composition-specific SPS consolidation, machining into electrodes, electrospark deposition on C1018 steel, and comparison of three versus six layers. Its mechanism is only loosely related through grain refinement and avoidance of bulk melting. The baselines include fusion-welded and untreated controls, but not the target's lower-temperature SPS samples or three-layer coating baseline. The proposed experiment includes relevant microscopy, hardness, residual-stress, corrosion, and cracking measurements, yet its falsification rule is a conjunction of several outcomes and lacks specified aggressive media, exposure duration, replication, effect-size thresholds, and acceptance criteria. Most importantly, the predicted service benefits have no cited support and extend beyond what the target evidence established.
